Computable Analysis / Gaussian integrals / Volumes in every dimension

A computation connecting geometry and analysis

Volumes in every dimension

A Gaussian separates into one factor for each coordinate. The same Gaussian, grouped by radius, produces the Gamma function. Comparing the two gives the volume enclosed by a sphere.

\[V_n(R)=\frac{\pi^{n/2}R^n}{\Gamma(n/2+1)}.\]

Here \(n\) counts ambient coordinates. We compute the volume of the ball \(B_n(R)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\sum_i x_i^2\le R^2\}\). Its boundary is the sphere of dimension \(n-1\); for \(R>0\), its area is \(A_{n-1}(R)=nV_n(R)/R\).

What is checked. Lean proves the coefficient identities, interval bounds, validity and representation independence of the volume formula for valid presentations of nonnegative inputs. Its identification with geometric ball volume, the Gaussian normalization, and the Gamma integral connection below remain proof targets. The browser is an exact rational implementation tested against Lean, not verified JavaScript. No Mathlib real numbers are used.

Compute a volume

Choose a dimension and an exact rational radius. Refinement continues until the rational enclosure is narrower than the requested decimal scale. No floating-point value of \(\pi\) enters the calculation.

Dimensions zero through 64; radii zero through ten. Enter a decimal or a fraction such as 3/2.

Inspect the rational bounds


The zero-dimensional convention is \(V_0(R)=1\), including \(R=0\). In positive dimensions the zero-radius ball has volume zero. Boundary area is displayed only for positive radius.


Two starting values, one recurrence
Checked coefficient algebra

\[V_0(R)=1,\qquad V_1(R)=2R,\qquad V_{n+2}(R)=\frac{2\pi R^2}{n+2}V_n(R).\]


Each step adds two coordinates. Write \(V_n(R)=c_n\pi^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}R^n\). Then \(c_0=1\), \(c_1=2\), and \(c_{n+2}=2c_n/(n+2)\). Every coefficient is rational. Odd dimensions need no square-root evaluation because the two occurrences of \(\sqrt\pi\) cancel.


\[V_{2k}(R)=\frac{\pi^kR^{2k}}{k!},\qquad V_{2k+1}(R)=\frac{2^{k+1}\pi^kR^{2k+1}}{(2k+1)!!}.\]


The double factorial multiplies the positive odd integers up to its argument. For the unit ball:


\(n\)\(V_n(1)\)\(\Gamma(n/2+1)\)Volume enclosure


The unit-ball volume reaches its largest integer-dimensional value at \(n=5\). The recurrence explains the eventual decrease: the next same-parity volume is multiplied by \(2\pi/(n+2)\). Changing the radius changes this factor to \(2\pi R^2/(n+2)\), so the maximizing dimension depends on radius.


Why the Gamma function appears
Analytic connection to formalize

For positive \(s\), the intended integral is
\[\Gamma(s)=\int_0^\infty t^{s-1}e^{-t}\,dt.\]


Integration by parts with justified endpoint and tail limits gives \(\Gamma(s+1)=s\Gamma(s)\). The starting values are \(\Gamma(1)=1\) and \(\Gamma(1/2)=\sqrt\pi\). The second comes from substituting \(t=u^2\) into the Gaussian integral. These identities supply precisely the integer and half-integer arguments needed here. See DLMF’s integral definition, recurrence and half-integer starting value.


The checked rational sequence \(g_n\) starts at \(g_0=1\), \(g_1=1/2\), with \(g_{n+2}=(n+2)g_n/2\). Lean proves \(c_ng_n=1\) for every dimension. The analytic identification still to prove is


\[\Gamma(n/2+1)=\begin{cases}g_n,&n\text{ even},\\g_n\sqrt\pi,&n\text{ odd}.\end{cases}\]


One Gaussian, two computations
Derivation and remaining bridges

First compute coordinate by coordinate. Product comparison and the one-dimensional normalization give


\[\int_{\mathbb R^n}e^{-\sum_i x_i^2}\,dx=\left(\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-u^2}\,du\right)^n=\pi^{n/2}.\]


Next group thin shells by radius. If \(v_n=V_n(1)\), their volume factor is \(nv_nr^{n-1}\). Substituting \(t=r^2\) gives, for \(n\ge1\),


\[\int_{\mathbb R^n}e^{-\sum_i x_i^2}\,dx=nv_n\int_0^\infty e^{-r^2}r^{n-1}\,dr=\frac{nv_n}{2}\Gamma(n/2)=v_n\Gamma(n/2+1).\]


Equating these expressions gives the volume formula. This argument is not circular if Gaussian normalization is first established independently against the project’s geometric circle-area value of \(\pi\). The square-to-triangle slope route is designed for that purpose.


Weighted Gaussian moments fit the same computation. For \(a>0\) and \(m>-1\), the target is
\[\int_0^\infty r^m e^{-ar^2}\,dr=\frac{\Gamma((m+1)/2)}{2a^{(m+1)/2}}.\]


General represented exponents need a constructed power function and effective endpoint control. The present calculator only needs natural-number powers and rational coefficients.


From rational boxes to exact values
Checked represented formula

The evaluator maps a nonnegative \(\pi\)-box and radius box to the two endpoint values of \(c_np^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}R^n\). Monotonicity proves enclosure and nesting. The public theorem NBallRaw.value_valid accepts every valid input presentation, including irrational radii and early boxes crossing zero. Internal reboxing replaces negative endpoints by zero and preserves every nonnegative represented value. NBallRaw.value_equiv proves independence of either presentation using RealRaw.Equiv. A separate computation theorem identifies the public evaluator with the endpoint formula on nonnegative boxes.


The browser computes \(\pi\) by the project’s rational Machin evaluator, \(\pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239)\), then propagates its bounds through the model. Lean-generated regression fixtures compare the exact fractions, including refinement stages and non-unit radii.


There is also new finite progress toward Gaussian normalization. With sampled cell masses \(a_i\), Lean proves
\[\left(\sum_i a_i\right)^2=2\sum_{i<j}a_ia_j+\sum_i a_i^2,\qquad 0\le a_i\le\delta\ \Longrightarrow\ \sum_i a_i^2\le\delta\sum_i a_i.\]


The diagonal contribution must be controlled when splitting a square into triangles. This estimate supplies that control as cell masses shrink; the slope substitution and compact-integral comparison are still needed.


Remaining native analysis. Prove the bounded Gaussian change of variables and full-line normalization; construct the Gamma improper integrals with explicit endpoint and tail schedules; compare finite Cartesian boxes with radial shells to establish geometric ball volume. The displayed derivation explains how those results fit together; coefficient algebra alone does not prove them.
